newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Advanced Micro moves down.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Advanced Micro moves down.

text.p: Technology company Advanced Micro Devices Inc lost more than two points in after-hours trade on Tuesday after posting second quarter earnings that misssed analysts' expectations, traders said.
Dealers said AMD traded at 36-5/8 after the bell, down from an unofficial close of 39-1/8.

The company reported a diluted share profit of $0.07 per share for the second quarter, compared with a loss of $0.26 per share for the year-ago period. First Call had forecast AMD earnings at $0.22 per share.
Motorola Inc shares, meanwhile, were held as the company released second quarter earnings of $0.62 per share, excluding a $170 million charge.

A First Call consensus of analysts' estimates put the technology giant's second quarter earnings at $0.56 per share, excluding the charge, which Motorola said it would take to exit the DRAM (dynamic random access memory) chip business.
The cellular and computer products company saw its share price surge to a new high of 83 during regular hours trading on expectations that it would meet ananlysts' views, if not surpass them.
The earnings releases followed a record high close for the Dow Jones Industrial average.
The Dow shot up to an unofficial close of 7962 on Tuesday, ahead 140 points, in a lift attributed in part to market confidence in strong second quarter earnings performances.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume also rose to 386,500, compared with 3,200 on Monday, and sesssion two volume hit 5,441,540, compared with 1,557,500.
